name: Centro de Procesamiento de Datos Sur

profile.campus: Banco Santander CPD Cantabria (Norte/Sur), Medio Cudeyo, Cantabria
profile.reading:
This is the Centro de Procesamiento de Datos Sur, the south building of Banco Santander's main Spanish data processing campus in the Medio Cudeyo area near Solares in Cantabria, northern Spain. It is paired with a companion building, the Centro de Procesamiento de Datos Norte, which stands about 290 metres to the north on the same site and is tracked separately in this registry. OpenStreetMap records both as low, heavily built structures, each with a single above ground storey sitting over two basement levels, a profile typical of hardened financial sector facilities where much of the technical plant is placed below grade. This south building is mapped as a data centre structure outright, while the north building is mapped as a building carrying a data centre telecom tag. Both were named by local mappers in 2018 and given their Banco Santander operator attribution in 2023.

Banco Santander inaugurated the Cantabria data centre on 16 December 2011, describing it at the time as the bank's fifth data centre worldwide, joining existing facilities in Madrid, London, Queretaro in Mexico and Campinas in Brazil, and stating that the new centre raised the bank's overall data processing capacity by 30 percent. Direct construction investment exceeded 240 million euros, with a further 104 million euros of public and private investment supporting the surrounding industrial area. The site occupies a parcel of roughly 300,000 square metres, leaving substantial room for later expansion, and the built facility was described at inauguration as spanning more than 6,000 square metres. Those figures describe the campus as a whole. No source found here breaks the site down building by building, so they are recorded at campus level against both rows rather than split by guesswork between Norte and Sur.

The centre is known locally as El Bunker, a nickname earned by its security posture, and it houses the bank's systems control centre, the Centro de Control de Sistemas.

Staffing at the site has not been stable. In February 2022 the Cantabrian press reported that the IT services contractor Indra Soluciones had dismissed about 35 percent of its Cantabria data centre workforce. That followed a decision the previous year by Santander Global Tech to move roles previously performed in Cantabria to Madrid, which regional union representatives contested on the grounds that much of the remaining workforce was already operating remotely and carrying positive performance reviews.

No IT load, utility power service rating, standby generation capacity or per building technical floor area has been published for either building, which is normal for a bank operating its own primary processing site, and this registry records none rather than estimating from investment totals.
